questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I prioritized an exicting culture and interesting society when choosing my study destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy but my experience is also that Japanese guidance in general are very lengthy and thorough. So it can also be quite overwhelming with all the information presented.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was both a information meeting at the dormitory and at the university. The university also had an exchange coordinator, who was very easy communicating with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Only one dormitory was available at my campus. My impression was that it was easy to get.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a shared kitchen, but honestly very dirty. However the university had a cheap cafeteria.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's quite small and the shared facilities are quite dirty. However, overall I was happy living there and the price was cheap compared to other options. Further, at my dormitory there was Japanese students living responsible for helping new international students adapting to Japan. This was helpful, given that English was not always common at the bank or city hall.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Was just given one excel-sheet with available courses and one excel-sheet to fill out with the courses desired. Some courses was limited and would result in a lottery if enough wanted to take these courses. Furthermore, it was only possible to withdraw from courses afterwards and not sign up for new courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A guide was provided and a link to a courses-database.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was unlucky in the sense that some of my desired courses had lectures simultaneously. Otherwise, I was able to get all the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't really have any.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: BA courses are not worth it and honestly reminded me more of high school. Some of my courses was also discussion or group based, but the general English level was quite low and thus negatively influenced the level of these courses. I wouldn't recommend this university for the academics.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I don't think I took similar courses to the ones I'm used to in UCPH. But I would say in general they prioritized quantity in terms of numbers of topics in a course over depth the selected topcis.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- 34333 Cross-cultural Seminar
- 36460 Language in Politics
- 34321 Cross-cultural Encounters 2
- 81507 Advanced Topics in Computational Intelligence in Games
- 33154 Databases
- 53432 Liberal Arts Seminar *
- 81487 e-Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Only e-Society was both an interesting and well executed courses. Very interesting and knowledgeable professor (Uwe Serdült), who organised many interesting guest lectures.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Quite many mandatory insurances in Japan. But not that expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is in general quite cheap in Japan. I was expecting to pay more in rent.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Few options for non-Japanese speakers. Furthermore, I never managed to get in contact with clubs that was open for english speaking student (Never answered my mails/calls).

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a guidebook with clubs and general activities. In general it seemed that many clubs existed.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I couldn't use any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just travel around in Japan. I had the most fun in the more rural parts of Japan, since they were less touristed compared to many sights in Kyoto.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, since it was cleary communication what was expected of you in terms of university. Difficult in terms of clubs and socializing with local students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In general it was quite difficult and many seemed quite introverted.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I would say that the most challenging part was the lacking english skills and something I didn't expect in english-taught courses at university level.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Looking beyond the university, the culture in Japan was just in so many was fascinating and interesting. Also an interesting society, so can recommend finding a good news source (I used The Japan Times).

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: My impression of the level was quite low, so don't do it for the academics. Further, use that there is so many interesting things to explore in the kanto region.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think that the guides provided is quite thorough, so I think everything can be found there.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to explore Japan. I don't think I have mentioned it so far, but there is also some amazing nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Accepting that my courses was quite different than expected and the level lower.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
